From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-14 01:35 -08:00
Subject: Re: sudden surge of 502/503/504 + 429 in APAC - initial diagnostics

TL;DR: observed burst from partner endpoint fanout + LB queue exhaustion. Taking actions now.

What I see (00:55–01:10 UTC):
- APAC edge LB (apac-proxy-2) CPU and conn-queue spiked; backend pool reported rising connection timeouts and several 502s when backend returned 502/ECONNRESET.
- 429 rate correlates with client retry bursts; tokens are being exhausted on per-client rate limits causing 429s under high concurrency.
- Autoscaler metric (effective_rps) underreported load due to an aggregation bug — caused slower scale-up.

Immediate actions enacted (01:28 UTC):
- Draining unhealthy targets from apac-proxy-2, enabled temporary additional capacity (scaled up pool by +30% from standby), and increased LB connection queue size.
- Rolling a temporary health-check relaxation (grace period +10s) to avoid premature backend evictions while nodes come up.
- Opened emergency routing policy to failover to us-west warm pool for non-data-residency-sensitive requests.
- Instrumented edge to add short-term 95th percentile request tracing to identify hot URI patterns.

Next (Ongoing):
- Grace to confirm autoscaler fix and push hotfix for metric aggregation.
- Recommend customer (Ana) reduce client retry concurrency to 4 and adopt a 500ms minimum backoff immediately.

Attachments: apac-lb-healthchecks.png (screenshot of connection queue spike).

Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-14 02:05 -08:00
Subject: Re: sudden surge of 502/503/504 + 429 in APAC - SRE notes

Adding SRE context and a suspected root cause.

Observations:
- Autoscaler bug: Effective RPS metric used for scale decision was being sampled at the ingress collector and truncated when spiky bursts arrived from partner fanout. This underreported sustained queue depth.
- When backend worker threads were saturated, the proxy returned 502/504 while the token-bucket rate limiter emitted 429 for clients hitting concurrency caps. Retries without backoff amplified the load creating a retry storm.

Immediate mitigations I applied (02:01 UTC):
- Hotfix: switch autoscaler aggregation window from 10s to 2s for ingress sampling to better capture spikes (deploying now).
- Edge rate-limit adjustment: tightened per-IP burst window and added a short global backpressure header to instruct intermediaries to back off (Retry-After: 2).
- Enabled emergency routing to us-west for eligible requests; pushed a config that excludes data-residency-restricted tenants (marked in account metadata).

Follow-ups:
- Postmortem required; collect sample traces and client retry logs (BrightLabs provided samples — thanks).
- Long-term: introduce adaptive token buckets and auto-throttle for downstream clients that show retry loops.

Grace O'Connor
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: SUMMARY: BrightLabs APAC incident (INC-2026-APAC-69) — actions and next steps

Executive summary and immediate next steps (for customer-facing timeline):

Timeline (PST):
- 00:58 UTC (00:58) — BrightLabs reported spike in 502/503/504 and 429s.
- 01:20 (Monica) — Incident opened and bridge stood up.
- 01:28 (Marcus) — Drained unhealthy LB targets, increased pool capacity +30%, relaxed healthchecks.
- 02:01 (Grace) — Autoscaler aggregation hotfix deployed; edge rate-limit tightened; emergency routing to US warm pool enabled (excludes data-residency-restricted tenants).
- 02:15 — Telemetry shows error-rate decline; continued stabilization through 03:00.

Root cause (current hypothesis):
- Sudden burst of requests from a partner fanout combined with a sampling bug in the autoscaler metric led to delayed scale-up. Concurrency-limited clients issuing rapid retries created a retry storm, amplifying backend queue exhaustion and 502/504 returns.

Customer impact:
- BrightLabs APAC tenants saw elevated errors during the ~00:58–02:15 UTC window; degraded performance for certain heavy endpoints.

Actions & asks:
- Customer: deploy client retry limits (<=4 concurrency) and 250ms->2s exponential backoff. Redwood SRE is available to assist with a hot client patch.
- Internal: Postmortem assigned, SRE to propose long-term auto-throttle and improved autoscaler aggregation.
- Commercial: Laura to prepare 15% one-month credit proposal; Sean to coordinate customer comms.

Attachments and artifacts: incident ticket INC-2026-APAC-69, logs (brightlabs-error-samples.log), screenshots (apac-lb-healthchecks.png), emergency mitigation playbook (emergency-mitigation-playbook.pdf).
